core_obligations: The first step (proof lines 2275-2277): with j the smallest index such that A_1 is contained in B_j, the induced map from the simple object S_1 onto the successive quotient T_j is an isomorphism.

The induction step (proof lines 2278-2288): the quotient A/A_1 carries two filtrations, one inherited from the A-chain and one obtained from the B-chain by adjoining A_1 to each term, and both have simple successive quotients; the induction hypothesis applied to these two filtrations produces the permutation of the remaining quotients.
Conclusion (proof line 2288): combining the isomorphism of the first quotients with the induction gives equality of the lengths and the required permutation of the multiset of simple quotients.
proof_roadmap: Match the first simple quotient of one filtration with a quotient of the other using a minimality argument.
Pass to the quotient by the first step of the first filtration.
Apply induction to the two induced filtrations.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Jordan-Holder theorem: two filtrations of an object of finite length with simple successive quotients have the same length and the same successive quotients up to permutation (statement lines 2259-2272). The proof is a complete argument: a minimality choice identifies the first simple quotient of one filtration with a quotient of the other (proof lines 2275-2277), and after passing to the quotient by the first step the two filtrations are compared by induction (proof lines 2278-2288). The non-formal content is the construction of the two induced filtrations on the quotient. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
